reader.requirement: At 85, when any argument-1 is not an integer (a literal with a decimal point, an item with fraction positions, a non-integral expression) FUNCTION SUM is a numeric function: its value keeps the fraction and it is refused where an integer operand is required, even when the value is integral.

construct numeric-function-identifier-operand-2002: at 85 a numeric/integer function written where an identifier stands (MOVE, DISPLAY) is refused COBOL0900; at 2002+ admitted. The arithmetic-expression path the returned value takes is not screened

probes.expected: refused: 2.0 is no integer literal, N/2 is no always-integer expression, D has a fraction position, so SUM is numeric (RV3) and §1989:A.2.3 bars it where an integer operand is required

probes.expected: all-integer arguments (items, literals, integer expression, nested integer function, ALL of an integer table) make SUM an integer function admitted as CHAR's integer argument: 65->@, 66->A, 101->d

probes.printed: at 85 COBOL0900 for DISPLAY FUNCTION SUM (1 2); at 2002 compiles
probes.expected: 85 refuses a numeric/integer function outside an arithmetic expression (§1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4)

reader.notes: SumScaled adds scale-aligned Int128 values checked (size-escaped, never wrapped); IntrinsicResultType.Resolve selects Integer only when every argument is provably integer (IsIntegerOperand reads the literal FORM, the item's integer description, a nested call's resolved type), else Numeric, and the CHAR screen honours it. No edition switch on the value or type path. Witnesses g85_bf40_08 and 1989-RV-A_2_42_4-3 MATCH at 85.
